nodes.name: Impregnation
nodes.procedure: First, nickel nitrate and spherical FC were added to isopropanol, and then the Ni-adsorbed FC was obtained after ultrasonic stirring for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: First, nickel nitrate and spherical FC were added to isopropanol, and then the Ni-adsorbed FC was obtained after ultrasonic stirring for 12 h

nodes.name: High-temperature pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The Ni-adsorbed FC undergoes high-temperature pyrolysis process where abundant defects are generated on the surfaces of the FC, serving as traps for anchoring Ni species (single atoms and atomic clusters).

unit_operations.name: Pyrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: abundant defects are generated on the surfaces of the FC during the pyrolysis process

nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Figure 1a, Ni/FC was prepared by a simple impregnation and high-temperature pyrolysis process... Subsequently, abundant defects are generated on the surfaces of the FC during the pyrolysis process

nodes.name: Ni on Vulcan XC-72R C preparation
nodes.procedure: Ni/C was prepared by replacing FC with Vulcan XC-72R C using similar impregnation and pyrolysis process as Ni/FC.
nodes.source_text: Surprisingly, there is a dramatic drop in the FE_CO (<10%) ... when FC is replaced with Vulcan XC-72R C

products_analyzed.value: GC for CO and H2, NMR for liquid

nodes.source_text: the highest FE_CO (92.0%) and suppressed FE_H2 (8.8%) can be observed for Ni/FC at an applied potential of -0.8 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), implying the excellent electrocatalytic performance of CO2 to-CO under acidic environment

nodes.description: CO partial current density comparison in acidic electrolyte at -1.1 V vs RHE
nodes.source_text: the partial current density of H2 for Ni/FC is limited to 3.50 mA cm⁻², in contrast, the CO partial current density of Ni/FC is 18.21 mA cm⁻² at -1.1 V vs RHE, which is 36.42 and 364.20 times those of Ni/C (0.50 mA cm⁻²) and FC (0.05 mA cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM images show Ni species exist as isolated bright dots (single atoms) and stacked clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images were conducted in Figure 1b,c. Apparently, a significant number of isolated bright dots and stacked clusters can be clearly observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-scale EDS demonstrates homogeneous distribution of C, F, and Ni elements in Ni/FC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic-scale energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) demonstrates the homogeneously distribution of C, F, and Ni elements in Ni/FC (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows Ni/FC absorption edge slightly higher than Ni foil but lower than NiO, indicating chemical valence closer to metallic state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Ni absorption edge of Ni/FC is slightly higher than that of Ni foil but significantly lower than that of NiO, suggesting the chemical valence of Ni is closer to the metal state.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows dominant Ni-C and Ni-Ni bonds with coordination numbers of 3.1 and 4.4 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the dominant peak of Ni/FC can be identified as the Ni-C and Ni-Ni bond with coordination numbers of 3.1 and 4.4 respectively (Figure 1f; Figure S6 and Table S2, Supporting Information).

properties.description: Fourier Transform Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS demonstrates presence of Ni⁻ and NiC⁻ species throughout three-dimensional space.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time of flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) further demonstrates the presence of Ni⁻ and NiC⁻ species in the entire three-dimensional space (Figure 1g-i).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines Ni loading amount on FC as ≈0.15 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading amount of Ni species on FC was determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS) to be ≈0.15 wt% (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS detects obvious F 1s signal indicating presence of F-C bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the obvious F 1s signal detected by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicates the presence of F-C bonds (Figure S5, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV-derived double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of Ni/FC is 13.0 mF cm^{-2}, Ni/C is 9.0 mF cm^{-2}, and FC is 3.0 mF cm^{-2}, correlating with ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: double-layer capacitance (C_dl), which correlates with the electrochemically active area (ECSA), was conducted... The C_dl value of Ni/FC (13.0 mF cm^{-2}) is significantly higher than those of Ni/C (9.0 mF cm^{-2}) and FC (3.0 mF cm^{-2})...

nodes.characterization_summary: Water contact angle of Ni/FC is 138.9°, much higher than Ni/C (64.6°), proving F increases hydrophobicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the water contact angle of Ni/FC (138.9°) is much higher than that of Ni/C (64.6°), proving that the presence of high electronegativity F can effectively increase the hydrophobicity...
